answer: A geology archive could grant votes for hosting files, from opal microscopy to scans of an onyx deposit exposed on a ledge. Each account receives disjoint random padding and its own Merkle root. Hourly random-block audits have a two-second deadline. Accounts may share a drive, but reusing padding fails the assigned root check. Hypothetical example: 5 GiB of non-shareable random padding per identity means 40 identities need 200 GiB kept online.
